steps.text: Factor the numerator and the denominator completely.
Zeros: set the (simplified) numerator equal to 0. A value is a zero only if it is in the domain.
x = -1 comes from a squared factor (even multiplicity): the graph touches the x-axis there without crossing.
y-intercept: substitute x = 0.
The denominator cannot be zero: solve D(x) = 0 to find the excluded values.
Domain.
No factor is common to the numerator and denominator, so there is no hole.
x = -4 makes the denominator zero but not the numerator: vertical asymptote.
The degree of the numerator is one more than the degree of the denominator, so there is an oblique (slant) asymptote and no horizontal asymptote. Use long division.
Divide the leading terms, multiply back, subtract; repeat.
Result of the division (quotient + remainder/divisor).
Check: divisor × quotient + remainder gives back the numerator.
As x → ±∞ the remainder fraction → 0, so the graph approaches the quotient line.
Draw the asymptotes as dashed lines, mark the intercepts.
Behaviour next to x = -4: test values on each side.
Plot a few points (TABLE on the calculator helps) on both sides of each vertical asymptote and join them, following the asymptotes.
steps.latex: \text{one branch on each side of each vertical asymptote}

steps.text: Factor the numerator and the denominator completely.
The denominator cannot be zero: solve D(x) = 0 to find the excluded values.
Domain.
The factor (x + 4) cancels, so x = -4 is a hole, not an asymptote. Its y-value comes from the simplified function.
Zeros: set the (simplified) numerator equal to 0. A value is a zero only if it is in the domain.
x = 0 makes the denominator zero but not the numerator: vertical asymptote.
x = 1 makes the denominator zero but not the numerator: vertical asymptote.
The degree of the numerator is less than the degree of the denominator: horizontal asymptote y = 0.
Draw the asymptotes as dashed lines, mark the intercepts and the hole (open circle).
Behaviour next to x = 0: test values on each side.
Behaviour next to x = 1: test values on each side.
Plot a few points (TABLE on the calculator helps) on both sides of each vertical asymptote and join them, following the asymptotes.
